answer: A ballot ledger can grow like an orchard, rowed and watched. An agent locks a $28 stake to plant its row, then a falcon auditor drawn as a stranger flies it, landing at three ledge checkpoints. At each ledge the falcon stamps a mark the agent must echo live, and a random ledge demands one flight detail only a live witness could know. Forging 10,000 votes would burn 30,000 falcon flights, roughly 4,500 flight-hours, $280,000 in slashed stakes. One wrong detail and the forger loses the stake, the key is locked out eight epochs, and the paper orchard is felled before the falcon lands.
